title: God rested (Genesis 2:1–3)
hook: on the seventh day God stopped and blessed the stopping

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pentecost and ordinary time, and your line: the ordinary is holy. That closed the circle of the year. Now ten days on sabbath and scripture.

When did you last stop? Not switch tasks. Not scroll on the couch while half-answering messages. Actually stop, with nothing left running. For some, the honest answer is: I can't remember. There's always one more email, one more load of laundry, one more thing. Now turn to the opening of the Bible. Six days of making: light, sky, sea, land, stars, fish, birds, animals, people. Every day, something new. Then the seventh day comes, and the story says God does something that sounds almost strange for God. Nothing. On purpose.
screen: `WHEN DID YOU LAST STOP?` → `SIX DAYS OF MAKING.` → `THEN, ON PURPOSE, NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Here's the text, in the King James Bible: "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it." The Hebrew word for rested is shavat: to stop, to cease. The word sabbath, shabbat, is linked to it: the stopping. God doesn't rest because he's tired. Isaiah says God "fainteth not, neither is weary." The rest isn't recovery; it's a choice. The work is good, and finished, so it's time to stop and enjoy it. Then something stranger: God blesses the stopping, and makes the seventh day holy. The Jewish thinker Abraham Joshua Heschel pointed out that the first thing in the Bible God calls holy isn't a mountain or a temple. It's a day. A piece of time. Later the commandment comes: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy." In Deuteronomy it gets a second reason: you were once slaves in Egypt. Slaves can't stop. So rest is freedom, and it's for everyone in the house: children, workers, strangers, even the animals. Jews keep that day from Friday sundown to Saturday sundown, with candles, a meal and rest. Christians share this first page with them, and tomorrow comes how Christians came to keep their own day. But it all starts here: before any command to rest, God rests first, and calls it blessed.
screen: `SHAVAT: TO STOP.` · `NOT TIRED. FINISHED.` · `THE FIRST HOLY THING IS A DAY.` · `REST IS FREEDOM.`

segments.voice: Let your hands go still in your lap, palms open, and stop: don't plan, don't fix, don't review your list, and if a task comes to mind, tell it: later. It may feel uncomfortable at first, even guilty; let it. If you pray, rest in God for these moments; if you don't, simply rest.
God rested. On the seventh day God stopped, and blessed the stopping, and made the day holy. Today's word.
Your line: rest is blessed. Even God stopped, on purpose. Day one hundred twenty-one, at rest.

howItsDone: Christians read the seventh day of creation as the root of the sabbath and of their own day of rest; churches and families set aside a weekly day for worship and rest, and Jews keep Shabbat from Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.

Making the world wore God out, so the seventh day was for recovery.
